Submitted. `PLAYGROUND/submission.md` is written and the validator can take it from here.

## What I delivered

`OUTPUT/answer.tex` (fragment, 8 pages compiled, 0 overfull boxes, all labels namespaced `p1:`), two vector PDFs, and `preamble.txt`. Lint passes.

All four TODOs implemented; notebook scaffolding copied verbatim; data loading reproduces every published statistic exactly (19,464 edges, 666 isolated, mean degree 5.106, 734 components).

## The result

My own **triadic** walk — `P(x) ∝ 1 + |N(cur) ∩ N(x)|` — wins **every column**: test MRR 0.7248 vs DeepWalk's 0.7207, country test macro-F1 0.6974 vs 0.6833. One embedding is best for both tasks, because both tasks on this graph are homophily tasks.

## Three things I'd flag as the substance of the work

1. **I ran the whole protocol at three seeds before claiming a winner.** The seven strategies span only ~0.013 test MRR, so without a noise floor the ranking would have been unfalsifiable. This materially changed a conclusion: on country **micro**-F1 the spread is just 1.7× noise, so the strategies are statistically indistinguishable there — only macro-F1 (3.9×) separates them. A reader of the micro-F1 column alone would conclude sampling doesn't matter.

2. **Both of my other two ideas failed, and I reported them as failures.** RWR (−0.0083) and degree-corrected sampling (−0.0086) are worse than plain DeepWalk. The degree-corrected failure is the interesting one: it was supposed to help *low*-degree users and did the opposite (+0.0099 at degree 8–15, −0.0199 at 2–3). node2vec's (p,q) buys nothing measurable over DeepWalk here.

3. **Cold start dwarfs every strategy effect** — Hit@1 runs 0.03 → 0.69 across degree buckets, ~50× the best-vs-worst gap. A random-embedding control I ran reproduces the cold bucket almost exactly, confirming those cells are noise rather than evidence about any sampler.

## Two things you should know

- **`\begin{itemize}` does not compile in this TinyTeX.** The default bullet requests TS1 font `tcrm1095`, which isn't installed; pdflatex dies at shipout producing no PDF. I bisected it and worked around it locally with `enumitem`. Other problems in this run will hit the same wall.
- I ran a single-strategy job to check reproducibility (it matched bit-exactly) and it clobbered `results_full.pkl`. I fixed the script so filtered runs refuse to write, regenerated the sweep, and rebuilt every table and figure from the restored data. No reported number changed — but the artifacts on disk now match the claims, which is the point. It's recorded in `submission.md` rather than quietly fixed.

`submission.md` also lists five places I'm genuinely uncertain — chiefly that triadic's margin is only ~1.3 sd on any *single* metric (my confidence rests on it sweeping all seven columns), and that node2vec is my own implementation, unvalidated against the reference.
